data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Biological evolution has no conscious aim of truth, whereas Popperian science explicitly aims at verisimilitude.","Survivors in nature do not offer themselves as guides for action in the same way scientific theories do for engineers."],"overturn_conditions":["If the filtering process (testing) is shown to be systematically biased against true theories.","If the aim of science is redefined as 'successful prediction' rather than 'truth approximation'."],"shared_structure":["Selection based on elimination of failures rather than confirmation of success.","Preference for the 'last man standing' without assuming future invincibility.","Distinction between 'having survived so far' and 'being safe forever'."],"source_memory_refs":["mem_survivor_bias_selection","mem_darwinian_fitness_vs_truth"],"transfer_claims":["Just as we bet on the species that survived a plague being more resistant (not immune), we bet on the theory that survived tests being closer to truth (not certain).","The rationality of the bet lies in the filtering process, not in a prophecy of future performance."]},"claim":"Popper's preference for the better-corroborated theory is defensible on his own terms as a methodological rule for 'verisimilitude-tracking' rather than probability-assigning; it avoids smuggling in induction by treating corroboration as a report of past performance (severe testing) that licenses the theory as the best current guess for truth-content, provided one accepts the cost of abandoning any guarantee that this guess will succeed in future practical applications.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If corroboration is interpreted as implying a higher likelihood of future success, the defense collapses into the very induction Popper rejected.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the agent requires a normative bridge ensuring safety for critical actions (e.g., bridge building), Popper's framework cannot provide it without illicitly importing probabilistic assumptions.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 'rational preference' is defined strictly as maximizing expected utility based on probability, then Popper's solution is irrational by definition.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The mechanism distinguishes between 'logical probability' (which Popper rejects as increasing with evidence) and 'corroboration' (a logical relation describing how well a theory has withstood attempts to falsify it). The preference is justified not by an inductive leap that the future will resemble the past, but by the rational aim of science to find theories with high verisimilitude (closeness to truth). Since a severely tested theory has survived where others failed, it is the only candidate remaining that has not been shown to be false; preferring it is the only non-arbitrary choice consistent with the goal of truth, even if this offers no inductive assurance of safety for action.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
